chunks: Ahmad ibn Idris and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Kufi, from Ubays ibn Hisham, from Abdullah ibn Sulayman, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about the Imam: has Allah delegated to him just as He delegated to Sulayman ibn Dawud? He said: Yes. And that is that a man asked him about an issue, so he answered him concerning it; then another asked him about that same issue, so he answered him differently from the answer given to the first; then another asked him, and he answered him differently from the answer given to the first two. Then he said:
"This is Our gift, so withhold or give without reckoning."
And this is how it is in the recitation of Ali عليه السلام.
I said: May Allah keep you well, so when he answers them with this answer, does the Imam recognize them? He said: Glory be to Allah! Do you not hear Allah saying:
"Surely in that are signs for those who discern."
"And indeed it is on an abiding road."

Then he said to me: Yes, when the Imam looks at a man, he recognizes him and recognizes his color; and if he hears his speech from behind a wall, he recognizes him and recognizes what he is. Indeed Allah says:
"And among His signs is the creation of the heavens and the earth and the diversity of your tongues and your colors. Surely in that are signs for the knowing ones."

And they are the scholars. So he does not hear anything of a matter that is spoken except that he recognizes it, whether one saved or one doomed. Therefore, for that reason, he answers them with what he answers them.

key_terms.الْأَئِمَّةُ: the Imams identified here as those possessing such discernment
key_terms.الْإِمَامِ: the divinely appointed Imam being discussed as possessing delegated authority
key_terms.الْعَالِمِينَ: the knowing ones, interpreted here as those endowed with true knowledge
key_terms.الْعُلَمَاءُ: the scholars, here referring to those possessing divinely granted recognition
key_terms.الْمُتَوَسِّمِينَ: those who discern signs and marks with insight
key_terms.فَوَّضَ: delegated or entrusted with authority by Allah
key_terms.مَسْأَلَةٍ: a question or legal/religious issue brought for answer

ai.seo_question: How does the Imam know people’s inner condition and why may he answer the same question differently?
ai.summary: This hadith describes a divinely granted authority and discernment given to the Imam, likened to what was granted to Sulayman ibn Dawud. It explains that the Imam may answer similar questions differently because he knows the inner state and condition of the questioners. It also connects this discernment to Qur'anic verses about signs for those who truly perceive and know.
